C1265.title: Man-in-the-Middle Attack Types Explained: Wi-Fi Spoofing, HTTPS Spoofing, SSL Hijacking, and DNS Spoofing
C1265.summary: A CSDN article outlines five common man-in-the-middle attack types: Wi-Fi spoofing creates a rogue access point with the same SSID to hijack user traffic; HTTPS spoofing tricks the browser into visiting a fake trusted site; SSL hijacking intercepts the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect to inject malicious links; DNS spoofing forces the browser to visit a forged address under attacker control; and email hijac
